I don't see changing TTD in response to this to be that viable. (The bomb is starting to activate...) We should treat the date as fixed barring breaking bugs and work for a solution implementable by release date. In particular, what Micah has laid out in the agenda: > If there are no non-censoring relays as of The Merge, we can launch with clients that have the MEV-Boost integration disabled or removed so anyone wanting to use it would need to run custom software, not something from the Core Devs. If there are some non censoring relays as of The Merge, we can make an effort to promote those (e.g., in documentation, blog posts, etc.) and suppress/discourage the usage of any censoring relays. Personally, as a solo staker, I will be waiting until there is a censorship-free relay until I run MEV-Boost 🤷‍♂️ I don't see any point in a delay. When we were concerned about a consensus client super-majority we didn't try and prevent people using Prysm, we offered better access to alternatives, guides to switching and helped people understand the problem. Nobody really knows what is the target of the regulation, it seems to have been made vague on purpose Sorry, bad wording. In my opinion, CLs should not have the ability* to connect to external builders when no "good" external builders exist. *The ability shouldn't be there by default. The term "good" is what is being debated about censorship. It's my opinion that an external builder that censors transactions is bad. I don't think that's the central debate, as (almost) everyone here agrees that censorship is bad for Ethereum. I think the key disagreement is whether we ship builder-api support _even if_ no non-censoring relays exist -- in the hope that some non-censoring relays appear, or that we may mitigate the danger of the existing relay by giving client devs some control over its use (rather than encouraging Flashbots or the staking pools to hack their own clients). IMO it's harm-minimisation with an option for improvement (ship builder support in clients) vs absolute intolerance (delete builder support from clients). My general belief is that the majority of proposers won't run non-stock software initially after the merge. Given enough time, I think *eventually* we'll see more and more people willing to run non-stock software but that will take a while. My hope is that if we refuse to launch builder API support until there exist non-censoring relays, we'll either see non-censoring relays show up to the party or we'll see PBS implemented with CR lists (or similar) before we see significant adoption of a non-stock validating software stack. I mean if I’d gone to all the effort to setup a relay and then clients pulled support in a really easy to revert pr right before the merge, I’d just revert that pr and put out custom builds immediately that people could easily use. So I think it’s unlikely that it will take time for people to customise clients to make this possible. It’s possible what will happen is a custom build of only the most popular clients will be provided and then we’ll have a censoring relay *and* reduced client diversity. I think you are not the average demographic of staker. 🙂 I think the vast majority of stakers will just download what is available on a releases page/list somewhere. I don't think building a custom client is hard, for the reasons you stated, but I think most people won't take the steps required to do it. Defaults are very powerful. I also think many stakers are going to be a bit hesitant to trust builds from unofficial sources. These are not absolute statements of course, but I think the segment of the staker population that will just use stock software at launch is significant. We already have majority of block producers running `mev-geth` in current Ethereum. I don't see why we wouldn't end up with the same thing rather quickly. Do recall that staking pools make up a super-majority of stakers. I’m saying the relay builder would just provide that download page. And most stakers follow guides which already build from source. The key thing is not making it a default, if users want to fork clients and add in new changes to it they can. If we know that the current state of feature will bring in more harm than good, the right thing to do would be to disable it. There have been multiple testnets that have run with mev-boost, the only relay that has been running/tested has been flashbots relay Yes, and it took years to get this adoption and many mining pools actually ran a mix of geth and mev-geth in their farms because they were so hesitant to run unofficial software across their whole stack. > If we know that the current state of feature will bring in more harm than good, the right thing to do would be to disable it. The point I’m making though, obviously poorly, is that users wouldn’t have to create a custom client or run unofficial builds. They run the official client released by the relay builder. excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
Option 1: Deliver official clients with the builder API implemented while we know that the only relays available to stakers are actively censoring.
Option 2: Deliver official clients without the builder API, forcing anyone who wants to use the censoring relay to source their software from unofficial sources.  Once non-censoring relays are available, add builder API support to official client releases and encourage users (socially) to use the non-censoring relay.
